title: Quantitative Estimation of Auxin, Siderophore, and Hydrogen Cyanide Production in Bacteria for Cucumber Growth
author: Zeinab Fotoohiyan
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Halotolerant PGPR bacterial strains Note: Our strains were isolated from field soil samples at a depth of 30 cm in the arid and saline regions of Jiroft (Kanarsandal, Jazsaleh, Anbarabad, and Karimabad areas) in Kerman province, Iran. All isolates were found to belong to the Bacillus genus, with isolate C8 identified as the most effective. Following PCR amplification of the 16S rDNA, an approximate 1,500 bp band was observed on an agarose gel. Amplicon sequencing was conducted by Bioneer Corporation in South Korea. After sequencing the amplified products, BLAST alignment was performed on NCBI to find a strain with a high degree of homology. The molecular weight of these sequence fragments matched that of the bacterial 16S rDNA fragment. Based on the BLAST results and the phylogenetic tree analysis, the C8 isolate was identified as Bacillus subtilis, as its amplicon sequence shared 99%–100% similarity with Bacillus subtilis. Bacterial codes: K: Kanarsandal; C: Karimabad; J: Jazsaleh; and A: Anbarabad.
Cucumber seeds (Royal cultivar) were obtained from the Agricultural and Natural Resources Research Center of Southern Kerman (Iran) Reagents

steps.title: Collect and process soil samples
steps.instruction: Collect soil from 30 cm depth at the four field sites, place each sample in a sterile plastic bag, add 10 g of soil to 90 mL sterile distilled water, shake at 100 rpm, 30 °C for 1 h, and prepare serial dilutions up to 10⁻⁵.

steps.title: Prepare media for isolation
steps.instruction: Prepare minimal agar medium and TSA medium in slant tubes (screw‑cap).

steps.title: Plate dilutions and incubate
steps.instruction: Spread‑plate 60 µL of each dilution onto minimal agar plates using a sterile glass rod, incubate at 30 °C in the dark for 48 h, then randomly select five colonies per rhizosphere sample and re‑streak on TSA plates for purification.

steps.title: Prepare stock cultures
steps.instruction: Inoculate purified isolates into TSA slants in test tubes, incubate 24 h at 30 °C, then store the stock cultures at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare NaCl gradient broth
steps.instruction: In separate 100 mL flasks of nutrient broth, add NaCl amounts of 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 35, and 40 g to obtain salinity levels of 0 % (control), 5 %, 10 %, 15 %, 20 %, 25 %, 35 %, and 40 % (w/v), adjusting the final volume to 100 mL with broth.

steps.title: Screen salt‑tolerant isolates
steps.instruction: Incubate the NaCl‑supplemented broths for 24 h at 30 °C, measure optical density at 660 nm, and select the 11 isolates that grow in the 40 % NaCl broth.

steps.title: Prepare PEG solutions for drought assay
steps.instruction: Prepare nutrient broth containing polyethylene glycol 6000 to achieve water potentials of 0.50, –0.15, –0.30, –0.49, and –0.73 MPa (using the published formula).

steps.title: Test drought tolerance
steps.instruction: Add 0.1 mL of each salt‑tolerant isolate to the PEG‑treated broths (three replicates per treatment), incubate at 30 ± 2 °C on a shaker at 120 rpm for 24 h, and measure OD at 660 nm; include control broths without PEG.

steps.title: Prepare auxin assay broth
steps.instruction: Make nutrient broth containing 0.5 % L‑tryptophan (500 µg mL⁻¹) and 2 % NaCl.

steps.title: Incubate for auxin production
steps.instruction: Inoculate the selected isolates into the auxin broth, incubate in a shaking incubator at 27 ± 2 °C for 48 h.

steps.title: Harvest supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the cultures for 10 min at 11 200 rpm, collect the supernatant.

steps.title: React with Salkowski reagent
steps.instruction: Mix 1 mL of supernatant with 1 mL of Salkowski reagent in a test tube, incubate at 27 ± 2 °C for 20 min in the dark; a pink‑red colour indicates IAA.

steps.title: Measure auxin concentration
steps.instruction: Read absorbance at 530 nm and calculate IAA concentration (µg mL⁻¹) using a standard IAA curve.

steps.title: Culture for siderophore assay
steps.instruction: Grow the isolates in minimum iron medium at 30 °C for 48 h.

steps.title: Add CAS reagent
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the cultures for 15 min at 81 600 × g, add 0.5 mL CAS solution to each supernatant, incubate at 30 °C for 20 min.

steps.title: Measure siderophore activity
steps.instruction: Measure absorbance at 630 nm and calculate siderophore production % using: % Siderophore = [(A_R – A_S) × 100]/A_R, where A_R is the absorbance of CAS + uninoculated medium and A_S is the absorbance of CAS + sample supernatant.

steps.title: Prepare HCN assay broth
steps.instruction: Prepare nutrient broth containing 4.4 % glycine.

steps.title: Inoculate and incubate for HCN
steps.instruction: Prepare a bacterial suspension of 10⁶ CFU mL⁻¹, add 3 mL to 100 mL of the glycine broth in a 250 mL flask, incubate at 30 °C for 48 h.

steps.title: Detect HCN with filter paper
steps.instruction: Soak Whatman No. 1 filter paper in 2 % sodium carbonate + 0.5 % picric acid, place the paper on the culture surface, then incubate at 28 ± 2 °C for 96 h; a colour change from yellow to orange‑brown indicates HCN production.

steps.title: Prepare Picosky medium
steps.instruction: Prepare solid Picosky medium (per recipe) and inoculate isolates onto the plates; incubate at 30 ± 2 °C for 5 days and observe clear halos around colonies.

steps.title: Liquid phosphate solubilization assay
steps.instruction: Inoculate the same isolates into liquid Picosky medium, shake at 3 rpm for 7 days at 30 ± 2 °C, then centrifuge 10 min at 16 100 × g, 25 °C, collect supernatant.

steps.title: Quantify solubilized phosphate
steps.instruction: Measure absorbance of the supernatant at 820 nm and determine phosphate concentration by comparison with a KH₂PO₄ standard curve.

steps.title: Select isolates for greenhouse trial
steps.instruction: Choose the four salt‑tolerant isolates showing the best auxin, siderophore, HCN, and phosphate‑solubilizing activities (e.g., K4, K14, K15, C8).

steps.title: Surface‑sterilize cucumber seeds
steps.instruction: Immerse seeds in 5 % sodium hypochlorite for 3 min, rinse 8–10 times with sterile distilled water, treat with fungicide captain (Wp50 %) for 3 min, then wash three times with sterile distilled water for 3 min each.

steps.title: Plant seeds in pots
steps.instruction: Place eight pre‑germinated seeds at 2 cm depth in each clean pot (21 × 16 × 16 cm).

steps.title: Inoculate seeds with bacteria
steps.instruction: Apply 3 mL of bacterial suspension (10⁸ cells mL⁻¹) to each seed.

steps.title: Set greenhouse conditions and design
steps.instruction: Maintain greenhouse at 28 °C, 75 % relative humidity, 12 h light/12 h dark; arrange a completely randomized factorial experiment with four salinity levels (control, 4, 8, 16 dS m⁻¹ achieved by adding NaCl to irrigation water), five bacterial treatments (no inoculation plus the four isolates), and three replicates; keep soil moisture at 70 % field capacity.

steps.title: Grow plants and collect data
steps.instruction: After six weeks, measure plant height with a millimetre‑graded ruler, fresh weight with a digital balance (0.001 g precision), dry weight after oven‑drying at 72 °C for 48 h, and leaf area using a scanner and Photoshop analysis.
